title: Character and Cocharacter Lattices
body_html:
Character and Cocharacter Lattices

To every algebraic torus \(T\) over a field \(k\) one associates two free abelian groups: the character lattice \(X^*(T)\) and the cocharacter lattice \(X_*(T)\). Together with the action of \(\Theta = \operatorname{Gal}(k_s/k)\), they form the complete invariant of \(T\) (see F-Tori Are Classified by Galois Modules) and, downstream, the foundation of root data.

Definitions

For a torus \(T\) over \(k\) of rank \(r\), with \(k_s\) a separable closure:

  • Character lattice \[ X^*(T) \;:=\; \operatorname{Hom}_{k_s\text{-grp}}(T_{k_s}, \mathbb{G}_m), \] a free \(\mathbb{Z}\)-module of rank \(r\).
  • Cocharacter lattice \[ X_*(T) \;:=\; \operatorname{Hom}_{k_s\text{-grp}}(\mathbb{G}_m, T_{k_s}), \] a free \(\mathbb{Z}\)-module of rank \(r\); elements are one-parameter subgroups.
  • Perfect pairing \[ \langle -, - \rangle : X^*(T) \times X_*(T) \;\to\; \mathbb{Z}, \] defined by \(\chi \circ \lambda = (z \mapsto z^{\langle \chi, \lambda \rangle})\) in \(\operatorname{End}(\mathbb{G}_m) = \mathbb{Z}\).

Both Homs are taken over \(k_s\); the Galois action is separate data, not built into the Hom. A separable closure suffices because tori split over finite separable extensions (The Minimal Splitting Field of a Torus); no algebraic closure is used.

Galois action

\(\Theta\) acts on \(X^*(T)\) by \(({}^{\gamma}\chi)(t) = \gamma\bigl(\chi(\gamma^{-1} t)\bigr)\) and compatibly on \(X_*(T)\); the pairing is \(\Theta\)-invariant. The action is continuous for the discrete topology on the lattices: each character is defined over a finite subextension of \(k_s/k\). This makes both lattices finitely generated continuous \(\Theta\)-modules, free as \(\mathbb{Z}\)-modules.

Two natural \(\Theta\)-equivariant identifications describe the points of \(T\) over \(k_s\): \[ X_*(T) \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}} k_s^\times \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} T(k_s), \quad \lambda \otimes x \mapsto \lambda(x); \qquad T(k_s) \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} \operatorname{Hom}(X^*(T), k_s^\times), \quad t \mapsto (\chi \mapsto \chi(t)). \]

Functoriality

For a morphism of tori \(f : T \to T'\) over \(k\):

  • \(X^*(f) : X^*(T') \to X^*(T)\) (contravariant);
  • \(X_*(f) : X_*(T) \to X_*(T')\) (covariant);

both \(\Theta\)-equivariant. Under the anti-equivalence of F-Tori Are Classified by Galois Modules, closed immersions of tori correspond to surjections of character lattices and surjections of tori to injections; the full dictionary for subtori and quotients is Subtori and Quotients via the Character Lattice.

Examples

\(T\) \(X^*(T)\) \(\Theta\)-action
\(\mathbb{G}_m\) \(\mathbb{Z}\) trivial
\(\mathbb{G}_m^n\) \(\mathbb{Z}^n\) trivial
\(R_{E/k}\mathbb{G}_m\) \(\mathbb{Z}[\Theta/\Theta_E]\) permutation
\(R^{1}_{E/k}\mathbb{G}_m\) \(\mathbb{Z}[\Theta/\Theta_E]/\mathbb{Z}\!\cdot\!N\) quotient of permutation
anisotropic \(T\) lattice with \(X_*(T)^\Theta = 0\) no non-zero fixed vector

Downstream role

For a connected reductive group with a maximal torus \(T\), the lattice \(X^*(T)\) carries the roots and \(X_*(T)\) the coroots; the quadruple \((X^*(T), \Phi, X_*(T), \Phi^\vee)\) is the root datum (root data). Valuation-theoretic invariants of \(T(k)\) over discretely valued fields are expressed through \(X_*(T)\), which is why the cocharacter lattice is the preferred working lattice of this topic.

lean_refs.name: Langlands.Tori.characterGroup
lean_refs.signature:
abbrev characterGroup (A : Type v) [Ring A] [HopfAlgebra R A] : Type v :=
  GroupLike R A

lean_refs.name: Langlands.Tori.cocharacterHom
lean_refs.signature:
abbrev cocharacterHom (A : Type v) [Ring A] [HopfAlgebra R A] : Type _ :=
  A →ₐc[R] AddMonoidAlgebra R ℤ

lean_refs.name: Langlands.Tori.diagCharEquiv
lean_refs.signature:
noncomputable def diagCharEquiv :
    Multiplicative M ≃* characterGroup R (AddMonoidAlgebra R M)

lean_refs.name: Langlands.Tori.diagCocharEquiv
lean_refs.signature:
noncomputable def diagCocharEquiv :
    (M →+ ℤ) ≃ cocharacterHom R (AddMonoidAlgebra R M) :=
  AddMonoidAlgebra.mapDomainBialgHomEquiv
